chunks: Al-Tawhid: Ibn Masrur, from Ibn A'mir, from his uncle, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban b. Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: Is Allah capable of inserting the Earth into an egg without the Earth becoming smaller or the egg becoming larger? He said: Woe upon you - Incapacity cannot be attributed to Allah. Who is more capable (of doing that) than the One who diminishes the Earth and enlarges the egg?!
ai.seo_question: Can God put the Earth inside an egg without changing their sizes?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Tawhid* illustrates the Shia theological concept of divine omnipotence (*Qudrah*) by affirming that God’s power is not bound by the physical laws of volume or mutual exclusion. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) counters the man’s doubt by emphasizing that the Creator who can make the Earth small can simultaneously make the egg large, thereby rejecting the notion that divine action requires compromising the attributes of the objects involved. This narrative serves as a foundational argument against anthropomorphic limitations on God’s ability to perform the impossible from a human perspective.
